column3: Close to the Greek; “stumbling blocks” is rendered “offenses.”
NKJV has “a millstone,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “a mill stone” with a different word.
NKJV includes “against you,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “If your brother sins.”
NKJV repeats “in a day,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has it once.
NKJV adds “I think not,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
Close to the Greek; “unworthy” is rendered “unprofitable.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV has “within you,” where the Greek may also mean “in your midst.”
